This week I want to talk about another artist, possibly one of the best modern artists in the last 20 years.

Don Hertzfeldt is a cartoonist and animator who is known for his particuarly unique and stylistic choice of animation. His animations always seem to be in a state of constant motion, like each frame was individually drawn, even in parts where there is no apparent motion. He also utilizes the medium of animation to its fullest, and does not limit the boundaries of his animation to the image itself, using conventional effects such as manipulating the paper he is working on, or the unique aspects of a medium like paint to create unique animations.

This is just his style, what I love about Don is his somewhat dark sense of humor, juxtaposed with his very serious outlook on reality and humanity. Many of his works have very strong thematic undertones, and while his latest work have been more artistic in scope than his earlier works, he has this strange way of adding an almost off cilter sense of absurdity that makes the interaction of events kind of awkward, yet still compelling.

His jokes are somewhat dry, and provide an amount of depth I don't see in most comedy, even in dark comics, as often times something can appear funny, but also be related to something you wouldn't consider humorous, leaving the viewer a bit estranged. Much of his work focuses on the existential, as well as the cynicism of artistry and contemplations of humanity.

He is a wonderful artist. And whether he cares or not, I find him to be an inspiration, even if he as an artist does not see himself as something to aspire to. I get the feeling he doesn't from his work. If I ever had the chance to tell him this, I would also apologize to him, because I would hate for people to aspire to be like me as an artist.

There isn't much out there to his name, but the little there is pure gold, and worth every second
